title: Gambhir Fires Back at Critics Ahead of Sri Lanka Tests as Coaching Record Faces Fresh Scrutiny
excerpt: India's head coach says the team is 'ready with every answer' as a challenging Test record — eight wins in 20 matches — draws mounting criticism from former players and pundits.
body:
• Gautam Gambhir has hit back at critics questioning his coaching approach, declaring India is "absolutely ready with every answer" ahead of the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka.
  • India's Test record under Gambhir stands at 8 wins in 20 matches (40% win rate), including series losses to New Zealand (0-3), Australia (1-4), South Africa (0-2), and England (first Test lost).
  • Former India batter Aakash Chopra has been especially vocal, noting Gambhir has "been losing and losing" and that the BCCI has given him everything he asked for with no excuses left.
  • India are currently fifth in the 2025-27 World Test Championship standings with four wins, four losses, and one draw in nine cycle matches.

Gambhir Breaks His Silence

India head coach Gautam Gambhir has delivered a pointed response to the chorus of criticism surrounding his Test cricket record, using a BCCI video shared on social media to declare that his team will back up words with performance when the two-match series against Sri Lanka gets underway.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=L-odP1ISvn0

"Come 15th morning, whether we are batting first, whether we are bowling first, we're absolutely ready with every answer, every question that's thrown at us, and every answer we are ready to give. So make sure we tick all the boxes from now on."

— Gautam Gambhir, India head coach

The first Test began on August 15, with the second scheduled for August 23. India enter the series without two key players — Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar have both been ruled out through injury.

The Numbers Behind the Criticism

Gambhir's red-ball record as head coach has become the focal point of sustained scrutiny. In 20 Test matches under his watch, India have won just 8 — a 40% win rate that falls well below the standard India's Test program maintained under predecessor Rahul Dravid.

The damage has been concentrated in high-profile series. A 3-0 home whitewash against New Zealand — India's first home Test series defeat in over a decade — was followed by a 4-1 loss in Australia. A 2-0 home series defeat to South Africa, featuring a record 408-run loss in Guwahati, added to the toll. Most recently, India lost the opening Test against England at Headingley by five wickets.

India's only Test series win under Gambhir has come against Bangladesh.

Critics Turn Up the Volume

Former India batter Aakash Chopra has been among the most vocal critics, arguing on his YouTube channel that Gambhir can no longer shelter behind excuses when the BCCI has fulfilled every request the coaching staff has made.

"Whatever team management is asking for, it is being given. So, if this is the case, then you also need to deliver the results. Period. There is no excuse," Chopra said. He has characterized Gambhir's tenure bluntly: "He has won 2 matches against Bangladesh and one against Australia. However, we lost three against New Zealand, three against Australia and one against England. He has been losing and losing."

Former India opener Sadagoppan Ramesh offered an even sharper assessment after the South Africa series, pointing to what he saw as a contradiction in Gambhir's approach: "You said even star players like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma must play domestic cricket to be considered for selection. Yet, you've never even coached a state team."

Gambhir's Defence

Gambhir has pushed back against what he sees as selective criticism. After India's ODI series win over South Africa earlier in the tour, the head coach argued that critics had ignored the context behind the Test defeats, particularly the loss of captain Shubman Gill to injury during the first Test.

"A lot was said because results didn't go our way. But no media outlet mentioned that we played the first Test without our captain, who didn't bat in either innings. We lost that match by just 30 runs," Gambhir said in Visakhapatnam. "Just because I don't make excuses in press conferences doesn't mean people should hide facts from the country."

He also took aim at an unnamed IPL franchise owner who publicly floated the idea of "split coaching" — a suggestion that separate coaches handle the red-ball and white-ball formats. "People who have nothing to do with cricket started making comments. It's important people stay within their domain," Gambhir said.

New Blood and the WTC Stakes

Gambhir used his pre-series address to welcome newcomers into the squad. Leg-spinner Saransh Jain appears set for a Test debut, while Auqib Nabi — the J&K sensation who helped his state win the Ranji Trophy last season — has earned a maiden call-up.

"We've got a couple of new guys in. To start with, Saransh, congratulations. You've worked extremely hard to be here. Make sure that you make your family and your country proud whenever you get that opportunity," Gambhir said.

The Sri Lanka series carries tangible consequences beyond pride. India sit fifth in the 2025-27 World Test Championship standings with four wins, four losses, and one draw. A poor result would further damage their qualification prospects for the WTC final, adding another layer of pressure on a coach whose white-ball record — including an Asia Cup, Champions Trophy, and T20 World Cup — has not insulated him from Test cricket criticism.
